title: Time and Work
desc: Problems on work done, individual days, combined efficiency, wages, and pipe-filling rates.
formulas: Work Done = Time Taken × Efficiency Rate
If A takes n days, A's 1-day work = 1/n
Combined 1-day work of A & B = (1/A) + (1/B)
Time taken together = (A × B) / (A + B) days

questions.q: A can do a work in 15 days and B in 20 days. If they work on it together for 4 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is :
A can lay railway track between two given stations in 16 days and B can do the same job in 12 days. With help of C, they did the job in 4 days only. Then, C alone can do the job in:
A, B and C can do a piece of work in 20, 30 and 60 days respectively. In how many days can A do the work if he is assisted by B and C on every third day?
questions.explanation: (1/20) (1/20) (1/10) (1/5) Whole work will be done in (3 x 5) = 15 days.

questions.q: A is thrice as good as workman as B and therefore is able to finish a job in 60 days less than B. Working together, they can do it in:
questions.explanation: Ratio of times taken by A and B = 1 : 3. The time difference is (3 - 1) 2 days while B take 3 days and A takes 1 day. If difference of time is 2 days, B takes 3 days. (3/2) So, A takes 30 days to do the work. (1/30) (1/90) (1/30) (45/2)

questions.q: A alone can do a piece of work in 6 days and B alone in 8 days. A and B undertook to do it for Rs. 3200. With the help of C, they completed the work in 3 days. How much is to be paid to C?
If 6 men and 8 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days while 26 men and 48 boys can do the same in 2 days, the time taken by 15 men and 20 boys in doing the same type of work will be:
questions.explanation: Let 1 man's 1 day's work = x and 1 boy's 1 day's work = y. (1/10) (1/100) (15/100) 15 men and 20 boys can do the work in 4 days.

questions.q: A can do a piece of work in 4 hours; B and C together can do it in 3 hours, while A and C together can do it in 2 hours. How long will B alone take to do it?
questions.explanation: (1/4) (1/3) (1/2) (1/4) (7/12) B alone will take 12 hours to do the work.

questions.q: A can do a certain work in the same time in which B and C together can do it. If A and B together could do it in 10 days and C alone in 50 days, then B alone could do it in:
questions.explanation: (1/10) (1/50) (1/10) A's 1 day's work = (B + C)'s 1 day's work .... (ii) (3/25) (3/50) (1/10) So, B alone could do the work in 25 days.

questions.q: A does 80% of a work in 20 days. He then calls in B and they together finish the remaining work in 3 days. How long B alone would take to do the whole work?
questions.explanation: (5/4) (4/5) Whole work will be done by A and B in (3 x 5) = 15 days. (1/25) (1/15) (75/2)

questions.q: A machine P can print one lakh books in 8 hours, machine Q can print the same number of books in 10 hours while machine R can print them in 12 hours. All the machines are started at 9 A.M. while machine P is closed at 11 A.M. and the remaining two machines complete work. Approximately at what time will the work (to print one lakh books) be finished ?
questions.explanation: (1/8) (37/120) (37/60) (1/10) (11/60) (23/60) So, the work will be finished approximately 2 hours after 11 A.M., i.e., around 1 P.M.

title: Profit and Loss
desc: Cost price (CP), Selling price (SP), Gain%, Loss%, Marked price and Successive discounts.
formulas: Gain% = [(SP - CP) / CP] × 100
Loss% = [(CP - SP) / CP] × 100
Discount = Marked Price - Selling Price

questions.q: Alfred buys an old scooter for Rs. 4700 and spends Rs. 800 on its repairs. If he sells the scooter for Rs. 5800, his gain percent is:
The cost price of 20 articles is the same as the selling price of x articles. If the profit is 25%, then the value of x is:
questions.explanation: Let C.P. of each article be Re. 1 C.P. of x articles = Rs. x. S.P. of x articles = Rs. 20. Profit = Rs. (20 - x). 20 - x x 100 = 25 x 2000 - 100x = 25x 125x = 2000 x = 16. Video Explanation: https://youtu.be/sidqvjUoZxY

questions.q: If selling price is doubled, the profit triples. Find the profit percent.

questions.q: In a certain store, the profit is 320% of the cost. If the cost increases by 25% but the selling price remains constant, approximately what percentage of the selling price is the profit?
questions.explanation: Let C.P.= Rs. 100. Then, Profit = Rs. 320, S.P. = Rs. 420. New C.P. = 125% of Rs. 100 = Rs. 125 New S.P. = Rs. 420. Profit = Rs. (420 - 125) = Rs. 295. (295/420) Video Explanation: https://youtu.be/bQA8SB8ycbw

title: Problems on Trains
desc: Speed, distance, time, train crossing platform/pole, and relative speeds of moving trains.
formulas: Speed (km/hr to m/s) = multiply by (5/18)
Speed (m/s to km/hr) = multiply by (18/5)
Time to cross stationary object of length L = (Train Length + L) / Speed
Relative speed (opposite direction) = S1 + S2; Same direction = |S1 - S2|

questions.q: A train running at the speed of 60 km/hr crosses a pole in 9 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: (5/18) Length of the train = (Speed x Time). (50/3)

questions.q: A train 125 m long passes a man, running at 5 km/hr in the same direction in which the train is going, in 10 seconds. The speed of the train is:
questions.explanation: (125/10) (25/2) (25/2) = 45 km/hr. Let the speed of the train be x km/hr. Then, relative speed = (x - 5) km/hr. x - 5 = 45 x = 50 km/hr.

questions.q: The length of the bridge, which a train 130 metres long and travelling at 45 km/hr can cross in 30 seconds, is:
questions.explanation: (5/18) Time = 30 sec. Let the length of bridge be x metres. (25/30) 2(130 + x) = 750 x = 245 m. Video Explanation: https://youtu.be/M_d8WufJWKc

questions.q: Two trains running in opposite directions cross a man standing on the platform in 27 seconds and 17 seconds respectively and they cross each other in 23 seconds. The ratio of their speeds is:
questions.explanation: Let the speeds of the two trains be x m/sec and y m/sec respectively. Then, length of the first train = 27x metres, and length of the second train = 17y metres. 27 x + 17 y = 23 x + y 27x + 17y = 23x + 23y 4x = 6y (3/2)

questions.q: A train passes a station platform in 36 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 20 seconds. If the speed of the train is 54 km/hr, what is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation: (5/18) Length of the train = (15 x 20)m = 300 m. Let the length of the platform be x metres. Then, x + 300 = 15 36 x + 300 = 540 x = 240 m.

questions.q: A train 240 m long passes a pole in 24 seconds. How long will it take to pass a platform 650 m long?

questions.explanation: Let the length of each train be x metres. Then, distance covered = 2x metres. Relative speed = (46 - 36) km/hr (5/18) (25/9) (25/36) 2x = 100 x = 50.

questions.q: A train 360 m long is running at a speed of 45 km/hr. In what time will it pass a bridge 140 m long?
questions.explanation: (5/18) (5/18) Total distance to be covered = (360 + 140) m = 500 m. (Distance/Speed) (500 x 2/25)

questions.q: Two trains are moving in opposite directions @ 60 km/hr and 90 km/hr. Their lengths are 1.10 km and 0.9 km respectively. The time taken by the slower train to cross the faster train in seconds is:
questions.explanation: Relative speed = (60+ 90) km/hr (5/18) (125/3) Distance covered = (1.10 + 0.9) km = 2 km = 2000 m. (3/125)

questions.q: A jogger running at 9 kmph alongside a railway track in 240 metres ahead of the engine of a 120 metres long train running at 45 kmph in the same direction. In how much time will the train pass the jogger?
questions.explanation: Speed of train relative to jogger = (45 - 9) km/hr = 36 km/hr. (5/18) = 10 m/sec. Distance to be covered = (240 + 120) m = 360 m. (360/10)

title: Simple & Compound Interest
desc: Principal, annual interest rate, time period, maturity amounts, and difference between CI and SI.
formulas: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100
Compound Amount A = P × [1 + (R/100)]^T
Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = P × (R / 100)^2

questions.q: A sum of money at simple interest amounts to Rs. 815 in 3 years and to Rs. 854 in 4 years. The sum is:
questions.explanation: S.I. for 1 year = Rs. (854 - 815) = Rs. 39. S.I. for 3 years = Rs.(39 x 3) = Rs. 117. Principal = Rs. (815 - 117) = Rs. 698.

questions.q: Mr. Thomas invested an amount of Rs. 13,900 divided in two different schemes A and B at the simple interest rate of 14% p.a. and 11% p.a. respectively. If the total amount of simple interest earned in 2 years be Rs. 3508, what was the amount invested in Scheme B?

Then, x x 14 x 2 + (13900 - x ) x 11 x 2 = 3508 100 100 28x - 22x = 350800 - (13900 x 22) 6x = 45000 x = 7500. So, sum invested in Scheme B = Rs. (13900 - 7500) = Rs. 6400. Video Explanation: https://youtu.be/Xi4kU9y6ppk

questions.q: A sum of money is to be distributed among A, B, C, D in the proportion of 5 : 2 : 4 : 3. If C gets Rs. 1000 more than D, what is B's share?

questions.q: It is being given that (232 + 1) is completely divisible by a whole number. Which of the following numbers is completely divisible by this number?

title: Number Series
desc: Identify arithmetic progression, geometric patterns, alternating sequences, and missing numbers.
formulas: Rule 1: Check difference between adjacent terms
Rule 2: Check square and cube progressions (n^2 ± k, n^3 ± k)
Rule 3: Check alternate series where even and odd positions follow separate rules

questions.q: Look at this series: 2, 1, (1/2), (1/4), ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This is a simple division series; each number is one-half of the previous number. In other terms to say, the number is divided by 2 successively to get the next result. 4/2 = 2 2/2 = 1 1/2 = 1/2 (1/2)/2 = 1/4 (1/4)/2 = 1/8 and so on.

questions.q: Look at this series: 7, 10, 8, 11, 9, 12, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This is a simple alternating addition and subtraction series. In the first pattern, 3 is added; in the second, 2 is subtracted.

questions.q: Look at this series: 36, 34, 30, 28, 24, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This is an alternating number subtraction series. First, 2 is subtracted, then 4, then 2, and so on.

questions.q: Look at this series: 22, 21, 23, 22, 24, 23, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: In this simple alternating subtraction and addition series; 1 is subtracted, then 2 is added, and so on.

questions.q: Look at this series: 53, 53, 40, 40, 27, 27, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: In this series, each number is repeated, then 13 is subtracted to arrive at the next number.

questions.q: Look at this series: 21, 9, 21, 11, 21, 13, 21, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: In this alternating repetition series, the random number 21 is interpolated every other number into an otherwise simple addition series that increases by 2, beginning with the number 9.

questions.q: Look at this series: 58, 52, 46, 40, 34, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This is a simple subtraction series. Each number is 6 less than the previous number.

questions.q: Look at this series: 3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 12, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This alternating addition series begins with 3; then 1 is added to give 4; then 3 is added to give 7; then 1 is added, and so on.

questions.q: Look at this series: 8, 22, 8, 28, 8, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This is a simple addition series with a random number, 8, interpolated as every other number. In the series, 6 is added to each number except 8, to arrive at the next number.

questions.q: Look at this series: 31, 29, 24, 22, 17, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This is a simple alternating subtraction series, which subtracts 2, then 5.

title: Letter and Symbol Series
desc: Alphabetical series, letter skips, reverse position values, and alphanumeric codes.
formulas: Position mapping (EJOTY): E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Y=25
Circular wrap: Z + 1 = A, A - 1 = Z

questions.q: SCD, TEF, UGH, ____, WKL
questions.explanation: There are two alphabetical series here. The first series is with the first letters only: STUVW. The second series involves the remaining letters: CD, EF, GH, IJ, KL.

questions.q: B2CD, _____, BCD4, B5CD, BC6D
questions.explanation: Because the letters are the same, concentrate on the number series, which is a simple 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 series, and follows each letter in order.

questions.q: FAG, GAF, HAI, IAH, ____
questions.explanation: The middle letters are static, so concentrate on the first and third letters. The series involves an alphabetical order with a reversal of the letters. The first letters are in alphabetical order: F, G, H, I , J. The second and fourth segments are reversals of the first and third segments. The missing segment begins with a new letter.

questions.q: ELFA, GLHA, ILJA, _____, MLNA
questions.explanation: The second and forth letters in the series, L and A, are static. The first and third letters consist of an alphabetical order beginning with the letter E.

questions.q: CMM, EOO, GQQ, _____, KUU
questions.explanation: The first letters are in alphabetical order with a letter skipped in between each segment: C, E, G, I, K. The second and third letters are repeated; they are also in order with a skipped letter: M, O, Q, S, U.

There are three series to look for here. The first letters are alphabetical in reverse: Z, Y, X, W, V. The second letters are in alphabetical order, beginning with A. The number series is as follows: 5, 4, 6, 3, 7.

questions.q: QPO, NML, KJI, _____, EDC

title: Blood Relations
desc: Decipher family trees, coded relations (A+B means father), and direct pointing statements.
formulas: Generational Chart: Grandparents (+2), Parents (+1), Self/Siblings (0), Children (-1)
Symbolic Notation: (+) for Male, (-) for Female, (=) for Spouses, (--) for Siblings
Maternal relations = Mother's side; Paternal relations = Father's side

questions.q: Pointing to a photograph of a boy Suresh said, "He is the son of the only son of my mother." How is Suresh related to that boy?
questions.explanation: The boy in the photograph is the only son of the son of Suresh's mother i.e., the son of Suresh. Hence, Suresh is the father of boy.

questions.q: If A + B means A is the mother of B; A - B means A is the brother B; A % B means A is the father of B and A x B means A is the sister of B, which of the following shows that P is the maternal uncle of Q?
questions.explanation: P - M → P is the brother of M M + N → M is the mother of N N x Q → N is the sister of Q Therefore, P is the maternal uncle of Q.

questions.q: If A is the brother of B; B is the sister of C; and C is the father of D, how D is related to A?
questions.explanation: If D is Male, the answer is Nephew. If D is Female, the answer is Niece. As the sex of D is not known, hence, the relation between D and A cannot be determined. Note: Niece - A daughter of one's brother or sister, or of one's brother-in-law or sister-in-law. Nephew - A son of one's brother or sister, or of one's brother-in-law or sister-in-law.

questions.q: If A + B means A is the brother of B; A - B means A is the sister of B and A x B means A is the father of B. Which of the following means that C is the son of M?
questions.explanation: M x N → M is the father of N N - C → N is the sister of C and C + F → C is the brother of F. Hence, M is the father of C or C is the son of M.

questions.q: Introducing a boy, a girl said, "He is the son of the daughter of the father of my uncle." How is the boy related to the girl?
questions.explanation: The father of the boy's uncle → the grandfather of the boy and daughter of the grandfather → sister of father.

questions.q: Pointing to a photograph Lata says, "He is the son of the only son of my grandfather." How is the man in the photograph related to Lata?
questions.explanation: The man in the photograph is the son of the only son of Lata's grandfather i.e., the man is the son of Lata's father. Hence, the man is the brother of Lata.

questions.q: If A + B means A is the brother of B; A x B means A is the son of B; and A % B means B is the daughter of A then which of the following means M is the maternal uncle of N?
questions.explanation: Because the sex of O is not known.

questions.q: If D is the brother of B, how B is related to C? To answer this question which of the statements is/are necessary? The son of D is the grandson of C. B is the sister of D.
questions.explanation: Given: D is the brother of B. From statement 1, we can detect that D is son of C (son of D is the grandson of C). From statement 2, we can detect that B is 'Female' (sister of D). Therefore, B is daughter of C.

questions.q: If A + B means A is the father of B; A - B means A is the brother B; A % B means A is the wife of B and A x B means A is the mother of B, which of the following shows that M is the maternal grandmother of T?
options: M x N x S % T
questions.explanation: M x N → M is the mother of N N % S → N is the wife of S and S + T → is the father of T. Hence, M is the maternal grandmother of T.

questions.q: Pointing to a photograph. Bajpai said, "He is the son of the only daughter of the father of my brother." How Bajpai is related to the man in the photograph?
questions.explanation: The man in the photo is the son of the sister of Bajpai. Hence, Bajpai is the maternal uncle of the man in the photograph.
